## Coverage of the spec

- Resources of the spec that are **not implemented**: `/hub`, `/listener` (`/hub` and `/listener/*`: no event notifications).


## Behaviour and deviations

- A customer is the role a party plays towards us: `engagedParty` is a `PartyRef` whose
  `@referredType` is the party's type (`Individual` / `Organization`); mandatory on
  create, must exist (422), read-only on PATCH (`app/api/customer.py`;
  `tests/test_api_parties.py::test_customer_round_trip`, `::test_customer_validation`).
- `name` is mandatory on create (TMF629's create schema); stored in `customer.name`
  (migration 0002).
- `status` is ours (a free string in TMF629): `Created` (the default), `Active`,
  `Inactive`. PATCH may set any of them; no transition rule. Any other value is a 422
  that changes nothing (`::test_customer_status_outside_the_enum_is_refused_on_patch`).

In these notes `::test_name` is a test in the test file named last before it. Hand-written: [`scripts/docs/api-notes/tmf629-customer.md`](../../scripts/docs/api-notes/tmf629-customer.md).


## Errors

Every non-2xx body is the TMF630 `Error`: `{"@type": "Error", "code", "reason", "message", "status"}` (`app/api/errors.py`), also for unknown routes, FastAPI's own validation errors and unhandled exceptions (500 says "internal error" only). Status codes: 400 malformed JSON, unknown or read-only attribute, bad query parameter; 404 unknown id or path; 405 unsupported method; 409 conflict with stored state; 415 wrong content type; 422 well-formed but invalid. 415 and 422 are ours: the TMF specs do not declare them. See [README.md](README.md#conventions).
